Guidance on the restless morning
The aim of this section is to explain the plain rules

Companion Animal Travel Desk
This section sets the standard for the safe, calm handling of traveling pets and their carriers across Aurelia Skyways services. Staff must treat every animal with steady care, speak quietly, and keep each carrier secure, upright, and clearly labeled during handover. A traveler may be assisted in a waiting area, but no pet is to be left unattended where a draft, spill, or crowding could cause distress.

At Port Isolde, <<FACT F021>>. Staff must follow the lounge entry controls exactly as issued and must not improvise access for convenience. At Vellmar, <<FACT F002>>. The named manager or delegated supervisor is the only source for local lounge direction, and the desk must record any change in condition, delay, or refusal of service before release of the carrier.

The ground team must move carriers carefully between services, using level support and clear communication, so that the animal is not jolted or exposed to avoidable noise. If a traveler such as Emil Lee or Rafael Adeyemi requests reassurance, the desk should answer in plain language and keep the process orderly. If a pet such as Poppy shows signs of stress, staff should slow the exchange, maintain distance from other animals, and notify the senior coordinator at once.

No one may bypass inspection, handling, or identification steps, even when the transfer appears routine. Any incident involving loss, injury, disagreement, or a missed handover must be entered in the log before the shift ends. The Companion Animal Travel Desk is expected to protect the welfare of each pet and to preserve a calm service standard at all times.

For guidance beyond this section, contact the senior coordinator through the established service channel.
